notes:
Summary: ThriveSignal (enterprise logistics/SaaS for last-mile routing) wants Dedicated capacity for real-time chat/dispatch + reranking candidate lists. Primary ask: firm throughput guarantees with clear concurrency caps and defined burst policy. They are sensitive to tail latency because dispatch decisions feed into downstream vehicle systems.

Throughput / SLA discussion (CRM shorthand):
- Customer target: sustained baseline >= 12,000 tokens/sec for core routing model (avg request ~ 35 tokens). Confirmed target originates from 250 req/s steady-state with expected spikes.
- Concurrency caps: propose contract concurrency cap = 400 concurrent requests (transactional p2p calls). They want per-tenant isolation within Dedicated pool (separate routing tags).
- Burst policy: allowed burst headroom = +50% sustained tokens/sec for up to 5 continuous minutes, once per 30 mins per region; automatic throttling after burst window. Need clear metricization (tokens/sec observed, burst_count).
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 140ms, p99 <= 250ms for generation path (end-to-end from request arrival to final token emitted). They accept longer latency for 2% of requests during global failover.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial recommendation (SE): 4x A100-80GB nodes dedicated to model family (quantized variant). Expected steady throughput per node ~ 3k–3.5k tokens/sec (model + sequence length distribution), plus autoscale to 6 nodes for burst headroom. Customer asked for mapping to physical GPUs and warm-cache sizing.
- Warm-up & cold-start: want guaranteed warm-KV cache for top 10k prefixes during SLA windows. POC must include cache-warm procedure and measurable warm-up time.
- Fallbacks & routing: agreed canary route: if Dedicated capacity approaches cap, route overflow to Redwood hosted with pricing uplift and explicit throttling policy. They want automatic fallbacks <2% of traffic ideally.
- Penalties: customer pushing for credit bands based on % uptime + missed tokens/sec guarantees (credits per hour of underprovisioning). Legal flagged that penalty language must be capped (they suggested 20% MSA cap).
- Observability: requires token-level telemetry, per-route cost breakdown, and alerting on sustained drops below baseline for >3 minutes.

Open items / POC criteria:
- Define exact tokens/sec measurement method (model-side vs ingress calc). Need alignment in POC acceptance tests.
- Finalize concurrency semantics (are streaming requests counted differently?).
- KMS: demonstrate envelope encryption with customer-managed key in VPC; security needs integration test.
- Pricing model for burst egress to hosted during overloads — finance to confirm uplift rate.

Quotes / call snippets: "We cannot tolerate 500ms spikes during peak dispatch windows — that causes missed pickups," - SVP Ops.
"If you can guarantee 12k sustained with the burst rules, procurement will sign MSA," - Head of Platform.

Artifacts referenced: proposal deck (Drive), SLA redlines (Drive), legal thread (Gmail thread:1782345), POC ticket INF-4827.

Next steps (short): finalize SLA redlines (legal vs their counsel) -> sign MSA -> run 14-day POC with agreed measurement script -> finalize reserved GPU count and commit term (12 vs 36 months).
